9. After notice respondents have filed the return by submitting that the Food Safety Officer collected the sample on 08.09.2015 and sent the sample for testing to the Food Analyst.
The Food Analyst submitted a report under section 46 of the Act of 2006 on 26.09.2015 i.e. before the expiry of shelf life of the sample.
The information along with the copy of the report was sent to the petitioners but they did not choose to prefer any appeal under section 46(4) of the Act of 2006.
As per the report of the Food Analyst, the product was found sub-standard, hence based on the Food Analyst's report sanction for prosecution has rightly been granted against the petitioner.

It is further submitted that section 66 of the Act of 2006 provides offences by companies and according to which every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the company shall be prosecuted.

Initially, the petitioner/company had sent the name of Manish Kumar as nominee but later on, they changed the nominee without informing the licensing authority, hence the sanction has been granted for prosecution against the petitioners.

The petitioners are free to raise all objections before the adjudicating officer and thereafter they have a remedy before the Tribunal which has been notified by gazette notification dated 25.10.2013 and 30.08.2013, hence the present petition is liable to be dismissed.

Advocate appearing for the respondents submitted that the sample was found to be sub-standard and the petitioners did not prefer any appeal despite receipt of information and assumed that the appeal cannot be preferred as the shelf life of the product had expired.
It is for the appellate authority to decide as to whether the product can be tested or not after the expiry period.
The prosecution can be launched against the petitioners based on the Food Analyst's report even if no appeal has been preferred.
The entire petition is based on the surmises and conjecture that the entire proceeding before the adjudicating authority is in futility in absence of any appeal to the designated officer.
The adjudicating officer is the competent authority to examine all the grounds raised by the petitioners in this petition.
After the decision by the adjudication authority, the petitioners may prefer appeal to the Appellate Tribunal, hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.

The Parliament in the 57th year of the Republic of India has enacted a law called the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 relating to food and to establish the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India for laying down science-based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption.

In exercise of powers conferred by section 91 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Central Govt. made the rules called the Food Safety and Standards Rules,

To decide this petition certain definitions and provisions of the Act and Rules which are required to be considered in the controversy involved required are surmised as under:-
13.
Under section 3(h) "designated Officer" means the officer appointed under section 36.
Under section 3(i) "Food Analyst" means an analyst appointed under section 45.

As per section 3 (n) "food business" means any undertaking, whether for profit or not and whether public or private, carrying out any of the activities related to any stage of manufacture, processing, packaging, storage,
transportation, distribution of food, import and includes food services, catering services, sale of food or food ingredients.

Under section 3 (o) "food business operator" in relation to food business is a person by whom the business is carried on or owned and is responsible for ensuring the compliance of this Act, rules and regulations made thereunder.

As per section 3(p) "food laboratory" means any food laboratory or institute established by the Central or a State Government or any other agency and accredited by National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories or an equivalent accreditation agency and recognized by the Food Authority under section 43.

14. Section 26 defines the responsibilities of the food business operator and section 27 provides the liability of manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers.
Section 31 provides licensing and registration of food business.
As per section 36, the Commissioner of Food Safety shall by order appoint the designated officer, who shall not be below the rank of a Sub-Divisional Officer.
Sections 37 & 38 provides Food Safety Officer and the powers of Food Safety Officer.
Section 41 gives powers to the Food Safety Officer for search, seizure, investigation, prosecution and procedure thereof.
Under section 42 the Food Safety Officer shall be responsible for inspection of food business, drawing samples and sending them to Food Analyst.

Under subsection (2) of section 42,
the Food Analyst after receiving the sample from the Food Safety Officer shall analyse the sample and send the analysis report mentioning the method of sampling and analysis within fourteen days to the designated officer for sanction.
Under section (3) of section 42, the designated officer after scrutiny of the report of Food Analyst shall decide as to whether the contravention is punishable with imprisonment or fine only.
In case he finds that the contravention is punishable with imprisonment, he shall send his recommendation within fourteen days to the Commissioner of Food Safety for sanctioning prosecution.

Under subsection (4) of section 42, the Commissioner of Food Safety shall, if he so deems fit, as per the gravity of the offence, may refer the matter either to a Court of ordinary jurisdiction or to a special Court.

sentences.text: The offences and penalties are provided in Chapter IX of the Act of 2006.
Section 51 provides punishment against the person who deals with the sub-standard food and the penalty may extend to five lakh rupees.

Section 68 provides the adjudication by the officer, not below the rank of Additional District Magistrate of the district and under section 69 gives the power to compound offences and thereafter section 70 provides the establishment of Food Safety Appellate Tribunal.

In the State of Madhya Pradesh, the District & Sessions Judge has been notified as Presiding Officer of the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal in the district in his civil jurisdiction vide notification dated 25.10.2013.
15. Chapter-VIII of the Act of 2006 deals with the analysis of the food.
Section 43 provides the establishment of laboratories, research institutions and referral food laboratory.
Section 45 gives power to the Commissioner of Food Safety to appoint such persons as he thinks fit having the qualifications as Food Analyst by way of notification.
The functions of Food Analyst are provided under section 46.

Under sub-section (1) of section 46 on receipt of a package containing a sample for analysis from a Food Safety Officer the Food Analyst shall examine the seal and thereafter cause to analyse such sample of an article of food within a period of fourteen days from the date of receipt of the sample and send the report.
Subsection (4) of section 46 provides an appeal against the report of Food Analyst before the designated officer who shall if he so decides, refers the matter to the referral food laboratory.
The method of sampling and analysis is provided in section 47.

For the sake of convenience sections 46 & 47 are reproduced below:

sentences.text: The main contention of the petitioners in this writ petition is that the report of the Food Analyst was received by them on 02.01.2016 with liberty to file an appeal under section 46 (4) of the Act of 2006 and rule 2.4.6 of the Rules of 2011 within thirty days but by that time the shelf life of the product had already been expired, therefore, they could not avail the statutory right of appeal to get the product analysed by referral laboratory.

The product was seized from the petitioner's dealer/
food business operator on 08.09.2015 by the Food Safety Officer and on the next date he has sent the same to the Food Analyst, who analysed the food and prepared the report dated 26.092015.

As per the Food Analyst's report the food was found to be 'sub-standard' as defined under section 3 (zx)
of the Act of 2006.
The said report was received by the Food Safety Officer on 12.10.2015.

Thereafter, he demanded requisite information from the petitioners vide letter dated 28.10.2015 and according to the petitioners by that time the shelf life of the product had expired i.e. within six months.
As per the information recorded in Form No.VI (Ex.P/3) frooti mango drink was bottled on 26.04.2015 and it was 'best before six months expiry period'.

According to the petitioners, the best before six months means the life of the product was only six months from the date of manufacturing and if it is to be analysed after the said date the report is bound to come as sub-standard.
In the Act of 2006, the sub-standard means the article of food shall be deemed to be sub-standard if it does not meet the specified standards but not to render the article of food unsafe.

As per rule 1.2.1 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011 the word "best before" means the date which signifies the end of the period during which the food shall remain fully marketable and beyond that date the food may still be perfectly safe to consume through its quality may have diminished.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Sub-rule (3) defines "date of packaging" which means the date on which the food is placed in the immediate container in which it will be ultimately sold.

Sub-rule (10) defines the word "use-by date" or "recommended last consumption date" or "expiry date" means the date which signifies the end of the estimated period under any stated storage conditions, after which the food probably will not have the quality and shall not be sold.

19. It is clear from the aforesaid definitions that after expiry date the food probably will have the quality and the safety attributes normally expected by the consumer and as per the definition of "best before" the date beyond that date the food may be perfectly safe to consume through its quality may have diminished, however, it becomes unsafe.
This is only an information but not mandatory to use before six month only.
It is not mention in the product or sample as whether it is to be used before six month from the date of manufacture or packaging.
Under rule 2.4.1 of the Rules of 2011, it is the duty of the Food Safety Officer to keep the sample in such safe condition to maintain the conditions suitable for analysis.
It is for the designated officer to take the decision whether after the expiry of the date the product is still referable to the laboratory for re-examination or not.
Admittedly, in the present case, the petitioners did not prefer any appeal against the report of Food Analyst and presumed that it is of no use after expiry of six months from the date of packaging.
The petitioners ought to have preferred an appeal, if so advised, and then it was for the designated officer to take a decision whether to refer one of the samples to the referral laboratory or not.

sentences.text: Under the Act of 2006 and Rules of 2011, there is no bar of taking action or decision for prosecution in case the person who did not prefer an appeal and he can be prosecuted based on the report given by the Food Analyst.
There is a limitation of 30 days for filing the appeal from the date of Food Analyst's report.
There is no bar under the entire Act of 2006 and Rules of 2011 for designated officer to take decision after expiry of shelf life of the product.

21. Shri Aniket Naik learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the provision of section 46 (6)
of the Act of 2006 and provision of section 24 of the Insecticides Act are para materia and has placed reliance over the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of Gupta Chemicals Pvt. Ltd.
(supra).

In the aforesaid judgment, the Apex Court has considered the provisions of Insecticides Act,
1968.

The Apex Court has quashed the prosecution due to sheer inaction on the part of the Inspector due to which it was not been possible for the appellant to have the sample examined in the central insecticides laboratory and the meantime the shelf life of the sample had expired.
The only difference is that under section 24 (4) of the Insecticides Act the accused is required to apply to the Court after launching of prosecution.
The Magistrate may in its discretion send the report for analysis to the central laboratory.
In the Act of 2006 and Rules of 2011, the right of appeal is provided before the stage of taking decision for prosecution by the designated authority.
The designated authority may decide to prosecute after the dismissal of the appeal if preferred by a person or no appeal is preferred.
The petitioners received the report of the Food Analyst but did not prefer the appeal within thirty days.

Thereafter, the designated officer has decided to go for prosecution on 17.06.2016.
22.

Even otherwise Section 12 provides that the Food Safety Officer while taking a sample for analysis may add to the sample a preservative to maintain it in a condition suitable for analysis .Therefore in a case where the sample of the food has been preserve such a way either by way of adding preservative or by keeping in cold storage than it cannot be presume that after expiry of shelf life same cannot be analysed.

For example if sample is taken just few days before "use-by date" or "recommended last consumption date" or "expiry date" and within such period it could be examine by the food analyst only and no time left for referral to higher laboratory by way of appeal than food operator would be free from any punitive action, certainly this cannot be intention of the legislature,
hence the provision has been made for prosecution on the basis of the report of food analyst.
23.

By way of this writ petition, the petitioners are also challenging the report of food analyst but they have failed to point out any error in the report, hence no prejudice has been caused to them by not getting any opportunity to file appeal.
In view of above discussion, I do not find any ground to quash the proceedings pending before adjudicating authority
.The petitioners are free to file an application before adjudicating authority for their discharge under section 66 of the Act of 2006 by giving name of their nominee.
24. Resultantly, the writ petition is dismissed.
No order as to cost.

Mr. Ashok Bhaves vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9
September, 2019
Author: Vivek Rusia

 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh : Bench At
 Indore
 (Single Bench : Hon. Mr. Justice Vivek Rusia)

opennyai_summary.facts:
After obtaining the aforesaid permission the Food Safety Officer filed a written complaint before the adjudicating authority.
8. Petitioners have assailed the impugned action of the respondents mainly on the ground that the report of the Food Analyst was communicated to them vide letter dated 23.12.2015 which was received by them on 02.01.2016 nevertheless by that time the shelf life of the sample produce had already been expired, therefore, they have been denied statutory right to prefer the appeal under section 46 (4) before the designated officer for forwarding one part of the sample to the referral lab,
Mr. Ashok Bhaves vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130631743/
2 hence now they cannot be prosecuted for violation of the provisions of the Act and the entire proceedings vitiates are liable to the quashed.
The Food Analyst submitted a report under section 46 of the Act of 2006 on 26.09.2015 i.e. before the expiry of shelf life of the sample.
The information along with the copy of the report was sent to the petitioners but they did not choose to prefer any appeal under section 46(4) of the Act of 2006.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In support of his contention he has placed reliance over the judgments passed by the Apex Court in the case of Gupta Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. & others vs. State of Rajasthan and another (2010) 7 SCC 735; Municipal Corporation of Delhi vs. Ghisa Ram AIR 1967 SC 970; Rajkumar Tinker vs. Food Inspector 2016 SCC OnLine MP 5089 and the judgment of this Court in the case of Prahlad Gattani & others vs.
State of M.P ILR (2012) MP 1454.
11.
It is for the appellate authority to decide as to whether the product can be tested or not after the expiry period.
The prosecution can be launched against the petitioners based on the Food Analyst's report even if no appeal has been preferred.
The entire petition is based on the surmises and conjecture that the entire proceeding before the adjudicating authority is in futility in absence of any appeal to the designated officer.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The adjudicating officer is the competent authority to examine all the grounds raised by the petitioners in this petition.
After the decision by the adjudication authority, the petitioners may prefer appeal to the Appellate Tribunal, hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.
The main contention of the petitioners in this writ petition is that the report of the Food Analyst was received by them on 02.01.2016 with liberty to file an appeal under section 46 (4) of the Act of 2006 and rule 2.4.6 of the Rules of 2011 within thirty days but by that time the shelf life of the product had already been expired, therefore, they could not avail the statutory right of appeal to get the product analysed by referral laboratory.
The product was seized from the petitioner's dealer/
food business operator on 08.09.2015 by the Food Safety Officer and on the next date he has sent the same to the Food Analyst, who analysed the food and prepared the report dated 26.092015.
As per the Food Analyst's report the food was found to be 'sub-standard' as defined under section 3 (zx)
of the Act of 2006.
In the Act of 2006, the sub-standard means the article of food shall be deemed to be sub-standard if it does not meet the specified standards but not to render the article of food unsafe.
This is only an information but not mandatory to use before six month only.
It is not mention in the product or sample as whether it is to be used before six month from the date of manufacture or packaging.
Under rule 2.4.1 of the Rules of 2011, it is the duty of the Food Safety Officer to keep the sample in such safe condition to maintain the conditions suitable for analysis.
It is for the designated officer to take the decision whether after the expiry of the date the product is still referable to the laboratory for re-examination or not.
Admittedly, in the present case, the petitioners did not prefer any appeal against the report of Food Analyst and presumed that it is of no use after expiry of six months from the date of packaging.
The petitioners ought to have preferred an appeal, if so advised, and then it was for the designated officer to take a decision whether to refer one of the samples to the referral laboratory or not.
20. On dismissal of the appeal by the designated officer or in case of no appeal has been preferred still the designated officer can examine the case on the basis of the sections under which the person has been charged and take a decision for prosecution either by the adjudicating authority or by a special Court, as the case may be.
Under the Act of 2006 and Rules of 2011, there is no bar of taking action or decision for prosecution in case the person who did not prefer an appeal and he can be prosecuted based on the report given by the Food Analyst.
There is a limitation of 30 days for filing the appeal from the date of Food Analyst's report.
There is no bar under the entire Act of 2006 and Rules of 2011 for designated officer to take decision after expiry of shelf life of the product.

In view of above discussion, I do not find any ground to quash the proceedings pending before adjudicating authority
.The petitioners are free to file an application before adjudicating authority for their discharge under section 66 of the Act of 2006 by giving name of their nominee.
24. Resultantly, the writ petition is dismissed.
No order as to cost.
